title: Long‐term radiographic marginal bone level changes around implants placed in periodontally healthy and periodontally compromised patients: A retrospective case series with 17–27 years of follow‐up
html:
Abstract

Background

The aim of this retrospective radiographic case series analysis was to assess the marginal bone loss (mBL) of implants placed in periodontally healthy (PHP) and periodontally compromised (PCP) patients after an observation period of at least 17 years.

Methods

A total of 32 patients (16 PHP and 16 PCP) rehabilitated with 57 implants (16 transmucosal and 41 submerged) with a mean follow-up of 19.5 years were selected for the analysis. All data were retrospectively extracted from the Department of Periodontology, University of Naples Federico II, Naples, Italy, and from a Private Practice in Piacenza, Italy. Marginal bone loss (mBL) was set as primary outcome. mBL was calculated by subtracting the radiographic vertical distance from the implant shoulder to the most apical point of crestal bone (IS-CB) at the time of crown insertion from the IS-CB at the follow-up. In addition, setting, implant location, smoking habit, sex, type of prostheses, emergence angle (EA), healing modality (transmucosal/submerged) and presence of marginal misfit were also collected.

Results

After a mean follow-up of 19.5 years, implants placed in PHP showed a mean mBL of 0.04 ± 0.69 mm, while around implants placed in PCP the mean mBL was 1.02 ± 1.96 mm. No statistically significant differences between PHP and PCP were found (p > 0.05). On the contrary, the frequency distribution of implants with mBL ≥ 3 mm was significantly different between groups (p < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis did not show a significant correlation between estimated variables and BL ≥ 3 mm.

Conclusions

Within the limitations of present study, the results indicate that past history of periodontitis in patients adhering to SPC may not affect the mBL around implants placed in PCP. However, the limited number of patients at each time point and the low statistical power do not allow for strong conclusions to be drawn.

Plain language summary

Dental implants are considered effective for the rehabilitation of edentulous patients in both PHP and PCP with high percentage of survival rate after an observation period up to 17 years. However, limited evidence on mBL around dental implants in PHP and PCP after a mean observation period greater than 15 years was noted. Hence, the objective of the study was to assess the mBL around implants after at least 17 years of follow-up. At different time points a few implants yielded a mBL ≥ 3 mm.
